newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RATING AGENCY TO RAISE CAPITAL EARLY IN '97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RATING AGENCY TO RAISE CAPITAL EARLY IN '97.

text.p: The first Polish rating agency Srodkowo-Europejskie Centrum Ratingu i Analiz SA, which was set up on Friday, wants to raise its capital to 2.2 million in 1997 zlotys from about 1.5 million, the firm's president said.

Wojciech Lipka told Reuters the company was likely to offer new shares ex-rights to Polish and foreign financial institutions possibly in the second quarter of 1997, increasing the number of shareholders to above 20 from the current 17.
"We have agreed to increase our capital to 2.2 million zlotys in the next few months ... I think it would be in spring," he said.
Lipka said the company, the current shareholders of which are mostly banks, wanted to see Polish and foreign insurance companies among its new shareholders.
He said the company already started negotiating with its future clients but declined to say when the first ratings would be issued.
"We are negotiating with several likely clients on issuing our rating, but I wouldn't like to say exactly when (we will issue a rating) ... we will try to do it as soon as possible," he said.
Earlier Lipka said first ratings were likely to be issued early next year.
The company wants to concentrate on the Polish market at first and later expand its operations to borrowers from other countries in eastern and central Europe.
